summary: Feed s172_triple to APM is degraded: 100% VLAN tags missing (VLAN 10,20 required), microbursts overload 10G port at 133% (13.30 Gbps), and 27.9% traffic remains ERSPAN-encapsulated. APM loses segmentation, drops during bursts, and cannot parse tunneled flows.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/aggregation is systematically stripping 802.1Q tags - 100% of 8286 frames arrive untagged while APM requires VLANs 10 and 20. Likely 'strip dot1q' or 'pop VLAN on ingress' enabled on broker ingress or SPAN source forwarding untagged.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot segment or filter by VLAN 10/20 (app tiers/tenants); all transactions collapse to untagged/default, breaking per-VLAN SLAs, dashboards and alerting and reducing detection coverage to 0% for VLAN-aware policies.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and forward original 802.1Q tags to the APM so it can correctly classify traffic by VLAN 10/20.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps APM port is fed bursty aggregate peaking at 13.30 Gbps in 1ms intervals (133% of capacity, 2 overloaded intervals). No load-balancing or rate-shaping in front of tool, so microbursts exceed line rate.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM NIC buffers overflow during bursts causing indiscriminate packet drops, incomplete TCP transactions, missed retransmits and skewed latency/throughput calculations; APM under-reports errors despite needing both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Spread flows across 2x10G APM ports with 5-tuple bidirectional hashing to keep per-port peaks <80% and prevent burst drops while keeping both directions of each flow together for APM.

findings.root_cause: 27.9% of frames (2310/8286) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel - remote SPAN/ERSPAN is forwarded through broker without decapsulation. Broker is not configured to strip ERSPAN/GRE.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees only outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE headers, not inner Ethernet/IP/TCP and application headers, so 28% of transactions cannot be decoded for response time, error rate or Top-N analysis.

recommended_fix.why: Terminate/strip ERSPAN at the packet broker to present inner packets to APM for full L2-L7 parsing without requiring tool-side tunnel support.
